{{nihongo|'''Ōkunitama Shrine'''|大國魂神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Mutsu Province]].

'''Ōkunitama Shrine''' (おおくにたまじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} in {{ill|Taira Suganami|Q128846854|qid=Q128846854}}, {{ill|Iwaki, Fukushima|Q274384|qid=Q274384}}, {{ill|Fukushima Prefecture|Q71707|qid=Q71707}}. It is a {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|lt=small Shikinaisha}} and its former rank under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}} was {{ill|Ken-sha|lt=kensha|qid=Q90139226}}.

=== History ===
[[File:Kabutoduka Kohun.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|[[Kabutozuka Kofun (Iwaki)|Kabutozuka Kofun]]}}{{small|One theory views it as the tomb of {{ill|Ishikami no Kuni no Miyatsuko|Q11585422|qid=Q11585422}}.}}]]

According to shrine tradition, in the {{ill|Enryaku|Q1373176|qid=Q1373176}} era of {{ill|Emperor Kanmu|Q314846|qid=Q314846}}, when Seii Taishōgun {{ill|Sakanoue no Tamuramaro|Q941979|qid=Q941979}} passed through this area under imperial order to subdue the eastern barbarians, he found an old shrine badly devastated. After asking local people and learning it was Ōkunitama Shrine, he prayed for victory; after the enemy was pacified soon after, he built a large shrine in thanksgiving.

Ancient ruins nearby include Nara-period temple remains and {{ill|Kabutozuka Kofun (Iwaki)|Q17990175|qid=Q17990175|lt=Kabutozuka Kofun}}. Because volume 10 "Kuni-no-Miyatsuko Honki" of '{{ill|Kujiki|Q2716751|qid=Q2716751}}' includes "{{ill|Ishikami no Kuni no Miyatsuko|Q11585422|qid=Q11585422}}," this area is inferred to have been their base, with this shrine considered their clan shrine and Kabutozuka Kofun their tomb. Also, {{ill|Iwaki Province (718)|Q1192809|qid=Q1192809}} was established for several years from {{ill|Yōrō|Q1373061|qid=Q1373061}} 2 ({{ill|718|Q23534|qid=Q23534}}), and this area is also considered a possible provincial capital site.

Later, in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}} it was ranked as small shrine. It was deeply revered by successive local lords, and in the {{ill|Edo period|ar|فترة إيدو|ast|Periodu Edo|az|Edo dövrü|bcl|Panahon nin Edo|be|Перыяд Эда|bg|Едо (период)|bn|এদো যুগ|bo|ཨེ་དོའི་དུས་སྐབས།|br|Marevezh Edo|ca|Període Edo|ckb|سەردەمی ئێدۆ|cs|Období Edo|cv|Эдо тапхăрĕ|da|Edo-perioden|de|Edo-Zeit|eo|Epoko de Edo|es|Período Edo|et|Edo ajastu|eu|Edo aroa|fa|دوره ادو|fi|Edo-kausi|fr|Époque d'Edo|gl|Período Edo|he|תקופת אדו|hi|एदो अवधी|hr|Edo (razdoblje)|hu|Edo-kor|id|Zaman Edo|is|Jedótímabilið|it|Periodo Edo|ja|江戸時代|jv|Jaman Édo|ko|에도 시대|lt|Edo laikotarpis|lv|Edo periods|mk|Едо (период)|mn|Эдогийн эрин|ms|Zaman Edo|nl|Edoperiode|nn|Edotida|oc|Periòde Edo|pl|Edo (okres)|pt|Período Edo|ro|Perioada Edo|ru|Период Эдо|simple|Edo period|sk|Obdobie Edo|sl|Obdobje Edo|sq|Periudha Edo|sr|Едо период|su|Période Edo|sv|Edoperioden|th|ยุคเอโดะ|tl|Panahong Edo|tok|tenpo pi kulupu lawa Eto|tr|Edo Dönemi|uk|Період Едо|ur|ایڈو دور|uz|Edo davri|vi|Thời kỳ Edo|war|Panahon Edo|wuu|江戶時代|zh|江户时代|zh_min_nan|Edo sî-tāi|zh_yue|江戶時代|qid=Q184963}}, donations of mikoshi, confirmation of documents, and construction of shrine buildings were successively made by the {{ill|Naitō clan|Q2975325|qid=Q2975325}} and {{ill|Andō clan|Q11451352|qid=Q11451352}}, lords of {{ill|Iwakitaira Domain|Q843782|qid=Q843782}}.

=== Cultural properties ===
; Kunitama Documents (Fukushima Prefecture designated Important Cultural Property)
: Ancient documents from the {{ill|Kamakura period|Q236205|qid=Q236205}} to the {{ill|Nanboku-chō period|Q264012|qid=Q264012|lt=Nanboku-chō period}}. Together with the Yatsuki and Iino document groups, they are important medieval historical materials. Among them, documents bearing sleeve seals of {{ill|Kitabatake Akiie|Q1036864|qid=Q1036864}} and {{ill|Ashikaga Takauji|Q297107|qid=Q297107}}, and the "old genealogy" identifying the founder of the {{ill|Iwaki clan|Q11474314|qid=Q11474314}}, are especially important.

=== Transportation ===
* From {{ill|Iwaki Station (Fukushima)|Q5353428|qid=Q5353428}} on the {{ill|Jōban Line|Q1369263|qid=Q1369263}}, take {{ill|Shin Joban Kotsu|Q11502130|qid=Q11502130}} bus bound for Nishihara via Natsui, get off at "Ōkunitama Shrine" bus stop
* 1 minute by car from the grade-separated junction of {{ill|Japan National Route 6|Q1038714|qid=Q1038714}} {{ill|Tokiwa bypass|Q11481556|qid=Q11481556}} and {{ill|Fukushima Prefectural Road Route 229|Q11593467|qid=Q11593467}}
